$comment: Every non-shell screen in supplement.product.kidney_liver.json. Shell screens SH1–SH6 are not authored here; they are identical in every programme. The person throughout is Marisol, 54, told at a routine appointment that her kidney results would be watched, with a fatty liver noted on a scan done for something else entirely. Every string is unreviewed. No string on any screen states or implies what a result means.

S01.headline: Seven sheets of paper in a kitchen drawer.
S01.sub: Longview is somewhere to put them. Your results, in date order, in one place, for as long as you want them — so that the next appointment starts from the whole story instead of the most recent page.

blocks.title: Kept by you, for years
blocks.body: Type a result in once and it's still there in 2031, whichever clinic you're with by then.

blocks.title: No opinion. Ever.
blocks.body: Longview will not tell you a result is fine, and it will not tell you it isn't. It doesn't know, it isn't allowed to guess, and pretending otherwise would be the most dangerous thing it could do.

blocks.title: Yours to take away
blocks.body: Export the whole file whenever you like, or delete it. Deletion is completed, not hidden from view.

S01.footer: Education and record-keeping. Longview does not diagnose, treat, prescribe, or interpret test results.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four points where having results on paper, twice a year, quietly fails you.

blocks.title: When the printout goes in a drawer
blocks.body: And the next one goes on top of it, and by the third you couldn't find the first. Two minutes of typing buys you a record that survives a house move.

blocks.title: When you can't remember what it was last time
blocks.body: Same test, same units, in date order, going back as far as you've entered. Just the run of numbers.

blocks.title: When you want to ask a better question
blocks.body: Walking in with four years of results and "has this been doing anything?" is a different appointment from walking in with one sheet. The question is still yours to ask — Longview only makes it easier to ask it.

blocks.title: When someone else should see them
blocks.body: A new clinic, a specialist, your brother. You read the exact page first, then you send it. Nothing goes on its own.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It does not read your results. It has no reference ranges, no flags, no colours, no ticks and no crosses. It will not say a number has gone the wrong way, because it does not know which way is the wrong way for you — only someone who knows your history can say that, and Longview knows none of it.

S02.footer: Education and record-keeping. Not a diagnosis, and not an interpretation of anything.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: The test names, the values, the dates, where the blood was taken, and anything you type next to them. These stay here.

blocks.title: Shared with your clinic
blocks.body: Nothing. Not by default, not on a schedule, not when a number moves. Longview has no link to Riverside or to anyone else, and it cannot acquire one without you setting it up and pressing send yourself.

blocks.title: You can leave
blocks.body: Export everything as a readable file plus a structured one, or delete it. Deletion is completed on your phone and on our servers, not hidden from view.

blocks.title: The thing most worth understanding
blocks.body: This is a filing cabinet with a good index. It is not a second opinion, and nothing you enter here is checked by anybody. If you type 58 when the sheet says 85, Longview will store 58 and say nothing — because it has no idea what either number would mean.

items.title: Remind me when a blood draw is roughly due
items.body: A date you set yourself. Longview does not know your appointments and does not talk to your clinic.

S03.footer: You can change either choice later in Settings.

S04.title: Your file
S04.headline: Hello, Marisol.
S04.sub: Nothing needs doing today. That is the usual state of this programme, and it is not a sign that anything has gone wrong.

blocks.title: If you feel unwell right now
blocks.body: Not puzzled by a number — unwell. That's the clinic today, or 911 if it's bad, and it has nothing to do with anything written on this screen.

blocks.foot: Across seven blood draws · the oldest is March 2023

blocks.title: One line left on the August sheet
blocks.body: It had three results on it and you typed two. The one still in the drawer is the AST. Two minutes with the paper in front of you and the sheet can go in the recycling.

blocks.title: There is no daily check-in
blocks.body: And there isn't going to be one. Longview asks you for something roughly twice a year, when results come back. Anything more frequent would be work invented to make the app look busy, and none of it would change what is in your blood.

blocks.title: Dr Shah · Riverside
blocks.body: Every question that begins "what does this mean" belongs here rather than in the app.

S04.footer: Works offline · Nothing here has been shared with anyone

S05.title: Your results
S05.headline: What the sheets said, in date order.
S05.sub: Copied off the paper by you. That is the entire contents of this page.

blocks.title: Longview does not read your results.
blocks.body: There is no verdict anywhere on this page — no colour, no arrow, no tick, no flag, and no reference range printed beside your number. A range shown next to a value is a verdict whether or not anyone calls it one, so Longview does not hold them at all. What these mean is Dr Shah's to say, and she has your whole history to say it from.

blocks.title: When and where
blocks.body: Copy the date off the sheet, not the day you're typing it in.

blocks.title: About the chart, and about the units
blocks.body: Seven eGFR results, oldest on the left, three and a half years apart end to end. It goes down, and in February it went up. Longview is not going to tell you which of those is which. The numbers are printed exactly as they were on your sheets and are never converted — if two clinics used different units, they are two different runs and you should say so to Dr Shah rather than expect the app to notice.

blocks.title: Also in your file
blocks.body: Three ALT results and two urine ACR results, on the same dates. Tap a chip above to bring up either run. Nothing is hidden — the list just gets hard to read with all twelve at once.

blocks.eyebrow: The only advice on this page
blocks.title: Anything here you want explained — ring Riverside and ask.
blocks.body: That is not Longview giving up. It is the only honest answer available: a number means something different depending on your age, your other conditions, what you were taking that week and what the last six looked like. Dr Shah has all of that. This app has twelve numbers and a date column.

blocks.title: If the clinic has asked you to come in
blocks.body: Go. Nothing in Longview changes that, and Longview has no idea what they saw. It cannot reassure you and it is not trying to.

blocks.title: Typos are yours to fix
blocks.body: Every value here was typed by hand and nothing checked it. Tap any row to correct it — the old value stays in the export with the date you changed it, so the record is honest about having been edited.

S05.footer: Typed in by you, off paper. Not received from a laboratory, not checked by anyone, and not interpreted.

S06.title: Learn
S06.headline: What the tests are. Not what yours said.
S06.sub: Six pieces, each one about a test or an organ in general. None of them knows your numbers, and none of them is written as though it does.

blocks.eyebrow: The one most people want first
blocks.title: What eGFR is, and why it is an estimate
blocks.body: 5 min · reviewed August 2026. Explains the test and the word 'estimated'. It does not say anything about the value you entered.

items: WHAT KIDNEYS ACTUALLY DO ALL DAY
FATTY LIVER: WHAT THE PHRASE MEANS
ALT, AST AND WHY LIVER TESTS COME IN SETS
WHY THE SAME TEST MOVES BETWEEN DRAWS
ELEVEN QUESTIONS WORTH ASKING AT A REVIEW

blocks.title: The line these articles will not cross
blocks.body: They describe the tests. None of them describes your results. An article can tell you what a laboratory is estimating when it reports an eGFR; it cannot tell you anything about the 58 on your sheet, and if one of them ever seems to, that is a defect and we want to hear about it.

blocks.title: Blood pressure, weight and drinking
blocks.body: All three come up constantly in kidney and liver care, and all three have their own Tether programmes with people who do it properly. Longview links out rather than writing a thin version.

blocks.title: What this library will not do
blocks.body: These explain. They don't prescribe. Nothing here names a medicine, a strength or a dose, and nothing here recommends a diet, a supplement or a course of treatment.

blocks.title: Why the dates are on the front
blocks.body: Anything not checked in eighteen months comes down rather than sitting here looking current.

S06.footer: Reviewed before it goes up, and dated so you can see how old it is.

S07.title: Support
S07.headline: A route to a person.
S07.sub: Which, on this screen, is not a consolation prize. Everything Longview refuses to tell you is something a person on this list can.

blocks.title: In an emergency
blocks.body: If you are seriously unwell — not worried about a number, but unwell — call 911 or your local emergency number now. Nothing in your file is relevant to that decision.

items: Reception takes result questions and rings you back
"Can you come to this one with me?"

blocks.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
blocks.body: Call or text 988 · English and Spanish · 24 hours. Waiting on results, or being told a long-term condition is being watched, is a heavy thing to carry quietly.

blocks.title: Two numbers missing from this screen
blocks.body: The National Kidney Foundation and the American Liver Foundation both run free patient helplines, and both belong here. We have not printed the numbers because we could not confirm they were current at the time this screen was written, and a wrong number on a page like this is worse than no number. They go in once somebody has checked them.

blocks.title: Exactly what would go to Dr Shah.
blocks.body: You are looking at the contents of the file itself, not a description of it. Nothing moves until you press send, and you can stop here.

items: All twelve results: test name, value, date, where taken
Which values you have edited, and when
Notes you typed beside a result
Any interpretation — because there isn't one to send

blocks.title: Sending this is not a clinical alert
blocks.body: It arrives as a document, not a flag. Nobody at Riverside is paged by it, nobody promises to read it by a particular day, and if something feels urgent to you then the phone is the right tool and this is not.

actions.label: Send the file to Dr Shah
Look at what's in it again

S07.footer: Crisis numbers route to United States services.

S08.title: Settings & privacy

blocks.title: Notifications
blocks.body: Detail is off. A reminder on your lock screen says "Longview" and nothing else — not a test name, not a date, not a number. Anyone who picks up your phone learns that an app reminded you, and nothing else at all.

items: February · a date you set, not one we know
Exactly as printed on your sheet · never converted
Nothing shared · you approve each send

blocks.title: Why one of those rows can't be switched on
blocks.body: There is no setting that makes Longview tell you what a result means. It isn't hidden behind a toggle or reserved for a paid tier. It does not exist, and the row is there so you never go looking for it.

blocks.title: Export everything
blocks.body: A readable file plus a structured one: every result, every date, every edit and when you made it. It stays on your phone unless you send it.

blocks.title: Delete everything
blocks.body: Completed, not hidden — your phone, our servers, and anything queued to sync. It cannot be undone, and three and a half years of typing goes with it. Export first if there is any doubt.
Education and record-keeping. Longview does not diagnose, treat or prescribe, does not interpret test results, and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified health professional.

S08.footer: Deleting Longview does not delete anything at your clinic. Your results still exist there.
